summary.headline: Chemplast Sanmar H1 FY22 revenue up 92% to Rs 2,633 Cr and EBITDA up 118% to Rs 498 Cr; Q2 EBITDA Rs 347 Cr, post-IPO debt repaid.
summary.overview: This was the company's maiden call after its August 2021 IPO. H1 FY22 consolidated revenue rose 92% year on year to Rs 2,633 Cr and EBITDA rose 118% to Rs 498 Cr, with margin at 19% versus 17%. Net profit was Rs 180 Cr against a loss of Rs 114 Cr a year earlier, after a one-off Rs 63 Cr finance charge from NCD prepayment and CCVL loan repricing. Management said the company is now net debt negative on a consolidated basis and that PVC pricing is in a structurally tight phase, though it declined to give medium-term per-ton margin guidance.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA grew through the quarter per management
vs loss of Rs 114 Cr in H1 FY21
Rs 26 Cr NCD fee write-off plus Rs 37 Cr CCVL loan repricing charge

financial_highlights.metric: Suspension PVC EBITDA per ton (H1 FY22)
financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 21,000 reported last year (as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (paste PVC and custom manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Specialty vertical revenue grew 81% YoY per management. Paste PVC: company holds ~45% market share and ~66,000 of India's ~80,000 tons production, running at full utilisation. Custom manufacturing revenue also rose YoY but was not quantified.

segments.name: Suspension PVC (CCVL, wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Capacity 300,000 tpa, with a 10% debottlenecking (~31,000 tons) due by end of FY22. Operates via imported VCM, an asset-light route with thinner value addition than integrated peers. Management estimates Rs 200 Cr quarterly EBITDA for CCVL, per analyst's calculation.

segments.name: Non-specialty (caustic soda, chloromethanes, hydrogen peroxide)
segments.commentary: Management said India is deficit in these products and the company holds a strong position in South India. Caustic soda utilisation is being restored to full capacity in FY23. No separate revenue or volume disclosure was given.

guidance_outlook: Interest and finance cost guided at Rs 40-45 Cr per quarter going forward, versus Rs 149 Cr in Q2 (including the one-off).
CCVL term loan repriced from 11.75% to 8.75% effective September 2021; the NCD interest of about Rs 18 Cr per month has ceased.
Paste PVC expansion of 35,000 tpa at Cuddalore, capex about Rs 256 Cr, commissioning by mid-FY24. Environmental permit is for 70,000 tpa in total.
Custom manufacturing capex of about Rs 340 Cr phased from FY22. Total announced capex programme is about Rs 600-620 Cr, of which about Rs 600 Cr is specialty.
Suspension PVC debottlenecking of 10% due by end FY22. A further expansion at the existing site could take about two years from final investment decision; environmental permit covers 600,000 tpa.
Effective tax rate about 17.5% at CSL (MAT credit, for a couple of years) and 25.17% at CCVL.
capex_capacity: Paste PVC: 35,000 tpa new capacity at Cuddalore, about Rs 256 Cr, on imported VCM via CCVL's import terminal; commissioning by mid-FY24; basic and most detailed engineering complete; ordering to start after environmental clearance is received (not yet received).
Custom manufacturing: new multipurpose facility, about Rs 340 Cr, phased from FY22; two new products commercialised in FY22.
Suspension PVC: 10% debottlenecking to about 330,000 tpa by end FY22; Cuddalore site could support tripling capacity; another 300,000 tpa would cost about Rs 750-800 Cr on the imported VCM route.
Paste PVC plant utilisation is full; FY20 utilisation was 100% for paste PVC, 82% caustic soda, 99% chloromethanes and 91% suspension PVC.
demand_pricing: Suspension PVC prices in India rose about 12-17% in October post Q2, and November import quotes also moved up, including from China.
Management expects a global PVC demand gap of about 5 million tons over five years (9.2 Mt demand growth vs 4 Mt capacity growth) per a cited industry conference.
India suspension PVC market about 3.4 Mt, with a deficit of about 2 Mt, expected to reach 4.3 Mt by FY25 (7.7% CAGR).
Chinese carbide-route PVC is under pressure from decarbonisation and the Minamata mercury convention; China's calcium carbide coal consumption target is -15% over four years.
Management says domestic PVC supply will not grow materially before 2025, given a four-year lead time for new capacity; ethylene availability is the historic constraint.
Management said demand remains robust; short-term affordability risk may shift some pipe demand to lower-quality pipes.

qa_highlights.question: Why is suspension PVC margin lower than DCM Shriram's?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the route is different: CCVL uses imported VCM with less integration, an asset-light model chosen for lower capex and faster time to market, and it could integrate backward later.

qa_highlights.question: How will the suspension PVC spread behave given Chinese supply returning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese futures fell after coal price curbs but physical PVC availability is tight; Indian prices rose 12-17% in October. It declined to give a per-ton EBITDA range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost outlook and the effective tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Quarterly interest and finance cost of Rs 40-45 Cr; CCVL taxed at 25.17%, CSL at about 17.5% on MAT credit for a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company holding cash and not repaying the Rs 830 Cr CCVL term loan?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company wants to stay liquid given the fluid environment, keep some debt for capital structure, and use cash for equity in capex and for opportunities. Trade payable credit is part of the industry model.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand suspension PVC by a further 300,000 tpa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India's deficit makes additional capacity a no-brainer; a further 300,000 tpa on the imported VCM route would cost Rs 750-800 Cr and could take about two years from final investment decision, but no decision has been taken.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 average realisation and October trend for specialty paste PVC?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the Q2 average was around Rs 150,000 per ton, and prices rose further in October without a specific figure.

risks_watch: Chinese carbide PVC policy and decarbonisation may shift global prices in both directions; management says some quarters will be lumpy.
Environmental clearance for the 35,000 tpa paste PVC expansion is pending; FY24 commissioning depends on it.
Feedstock and VCM import dependency; payables are largely dollar-denominated (about Rs 2,000 Cr), with forex covered at order placement.
Cash deployment decision (about Rs 1,000 Cr+ net cash) and whether the company commits to further suspension PVC capacity.
Q3 EBITDA trend versus the exit rate, which management declined to give monthly; interest cost guidance at Rs 40-45 Cr per quarter.
Demand affordability risk in pipes if prices stay high, possibly shifting to lower-quality pipe.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the sector outlook for PVC and specialty chemicals, but guarded on near-term numbers: management declined to give per-ton margin ranges, exit EBITDA, paste PVC realisation figures, custom manufacturing revenue, and a timeline for further suspension PVC capex.
key_quotes: There is a stage shift in terms of industry dynamic.
We are not circumspect on capital.

Domestic supply is not going up at least until 2025 because even if somebody tried today, they will take at least for getting the approvals and then starting the build, it will take at least four years.
